newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian "Lazarus" was given up for dead.
newsitem.headline: Colombian "Lazarus" was given up for dead.

text.p: One of 70 Colombian soldiers freed by leftist rebels after months of captivity had been given up for dead and officially "buried" last year, Bogota's El Tiempo newspaper said on Monday.

It said the military had sent the family of Angedis Morales what were believed to be his decomposed remains last year after guerrillas attacked an army base in southwest Colombia, killing 30 soldiers and capturing 60 others.
But the corpse, which Morales' family buried and mourned over, was exhumed months after the burial and identified as that of another soldier killed in the attack, El Tiempo said.
Military spokesmen could not be reached for immediate comment on the report of mistaken identification.

But El Tiempo said Morales' mother and father were on hand for his release on Sunday by the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC) in southern Caqueta province, where the rebels freed the 60 troops and another 10 marines they were holding.
"He's here, I have him in my arms," his mother Damarias told the paper of the son she said had risen from the dead.
